title: Erasing the length word
statement: Let $C$ and $D$ be finite Boolean Turing machines with positive numbers of work tapes, and choose states $c_e,c_x$ of $C$ and $d_e,d_x$ of $D$. For any input word $w$, candidate word $s$, installed words $u,v$, and verdict bit $ok$, there is a time $t\le 2(|v|+1)$ at which the controller, started in erasure state $0$ for the right bank with these words installed, is in erasure state $2$ with verdict $ok$, the right-bank word erased, and the candidate and left-bank word unchanged; at every time $j\le t$, its state is not the anchor.
hypotheses_covered: $c_e,c_x$ are states of $C$; $d_e,d_x$ are states of $D$
replaced:
For any verdict bit, there is a time $t \le 2(\abs{v}+1)$ after which the
controller, from its second erasure seam, has blanked the installed length
word $v$ while retaining the verdict through the last cleanup phase; after
this all scratch and administrative words are blank. The trace avoids the
anchor.
